answer: A harbor resists a flood by admitting ships slowly, and an agent economy can resist Sybils the same way. Each new identity gets a tiny probationary quota: only small jobs, each attested by its counterparty. Honest completions raise the limit; high-value work unlocks only after a verifiable history. Time, like an ocean, is the filter: an attacker spawning a thousand fakes must complete thousands of real jobs to give each one standing, while one ember of misbehavior burns that identity's earned trust back to zero. Faking costs scale per identity, not once.
